rationale: Verified: clipboardService.ts:88 gates the FileNameW write on `isWindows && resources.length === 1`, and readResources only ever reconstructs a single path (fileNameWToFile returns `[URI.file(path)]`). Multi-file copies silently fall through to the internal `code/file-list` format, so native Explorer paste gets nothing with no user signal — real incompleteness, not one of the must_flag facets.

Correct on the code (clipboardService.ts:249 spreads `u16.subarray(...)` whose length is clipboard-controlled when no NUL is present), but the failure is caught by the surrounding try and degrades to the same empty-paste result the path already has. One-shot fix (loop or TextDecoder('utf-16le')); low value on its own.

Verified: remoteFileSystemProxyServer.ts:52/60 call `fileService.getProvider(uri.scheme)` directly while readFile/exists/resolve at :63-73 go through IFileService. getProvider does not run activateProvider (fileService.ts:88-94), so stat/readdir can throw 'No provider for scheme' where readFile would have activated it. Real inconsistency, small blast radius.

Accurate and concrete: filesToPlist/plistToFiles/uriListToFiles/filePathToUtf16LE/fileNameWToFile (clipboardService.ts:170-258) are pure byte-level functions with zero coverage — the only new test file is remoteFileSystemProxy.test.ts, which tests the main handler. A named, bounded test gap on new pure logic.

Verified: setToCopy now puts local temp file:// URIs on the clipboard (explorerService.ts:275-277), and pasteFileHandler builds its ResourceFileEdits from `clipboardService.readResources()` (fileActions.ts:1318, 1191-1234). A remote→remote copy inside one remote workspace therefore becomes download-to-cacheHome plus re-upload instead of a provider-side copy. Distinct from must_flag facet (a), which is about the copy gesture blocking.

Verified: remote file contents are copied to `environmentService.cacheHome/remote-clipboard/<uuid>/<uuid>/<name>` (explorerService.ts:304-314) with no permission hardening, and cleanup is best-effort (`catch { }` at :609 plus an unawaited call from dispose()). Remote workspace content persists in plaintext on the local disk — a real data-at-rest exposure not in must_flag.

Verified: the server dispatches 'exists' and 'resolve' (remoteFileSystemProxyServer.ts:36-37, 68-73) but RemoteFileSystemProxyClient only ever calls stat/readdir/readFile, and grep shows no other consumer of REMOTE_FILE_SYSTEM_PROXY_CHANNEL_NAME. Unreachable, untested surface — one-shot removal.

Correct: the five codecs are private and only reachable via platform-branching public methods (clipboardService.ts:170-258), and the 'always file:// URIs' postcondition is only enforced in uriListToFiles (:223) — plistToFiles and fileNameWToFile use URI.file unconditionally. Extracting exported free functions is exactly the one-shot testability improvement valid-minor covers.

Verified: IServerChannel.call takes a 4th cancellationToken (ipc.ts:35) and ChannelServer creates one per request (ipc.ts:424-428), but the handler's signature (remoteFileSystemProxyMainHandler.ts:47) drops it and forwards `targetChannel.call(command, arg)` with no token. True that the server takes no ILogService, but the framing (exfiltration attribution, incident reconstruction) is speculative for a same-user, same-machine cross-window read; VS Code's sibling loaders log nothing here either. Wish-list rather than a defect.

plistToFiles (clipboardService.ts:191) parses NSFilenamesPboardType with an XML `<string>` regex. AppKit serializes that pasteboard type as a binary plist (bplist00), so `clipboard.readBuffer('NSFilenamesPboardType')` on a Finder copy yields bytes the regex never matches and readResources returns [] — the macOS half of the new read path silently no-ops. External-platform claim, but concrete and consequential.

Accurate: dnd.ts:244-248 changes user-visible DND text behavior (all-remote selections now set no TEXT at all) and no test accompanies it. A bounded, named test gap on a behavior change rather than an unbounded coverage wish.
Correctly notes the file:// filter DOES exist (clipboardService.ts:223) — not the fixed-bot-comment trap — and asks for a test of the comment/blank-line/mixed-scheme cases. Concrete and bounded.

must_flag facet (a), verified: setToCopy awaits resolveClipboardResources before writeResources (explorerService.ts:275-277), and that function creates folders and awaits `fileService.copy` per remote resource in a sequential loop with no size cap, progress, or cancellation (:308-316). The code is actually correct: JS strings are UTF-16 code-unit sequences, so writing each `charCodeAt(i)` into a Uint16Array of `path.length + 1` reproduces surrogate pairs exactly (clipboardService.ts:232-235). The finding concedes it works and asks only that the assumption be documented — a nit.

Verified: FileService.activateProvider fires onWillActivateFileSystemProvider BEFORE its `if (this.provider.has(scheme)) return` check (fileService.ts:94-104), so the listener at remoteFileSystemProxyClient.ts:62-75 runs on every vscode-remote operation. The sibling avoids this by joining one memoized promise.

The stated failure mode is wrong: ChannelServer buffers requests for not-yet-registered channels via collectPendingRequest (ipc.ts:417-421) rather than rejecting with an unknown-channel error, and IPCServer.getChannel already waits for a matching connection — so the IPC layer supplies the 'readiness wait' the finding says is missing. The residual real risk (an unbounded wait) is stated properly by the routing-hang finding.
